correctness.rationale: Model densities integrate to one; H=F-v strictly concave on each of two runoff-volume segments. Boundary values and one-sided endpoint derivatives yield necessary and sufficient strict source-share interval, and strict concavity at its lower endpoint proves nonemptiness. U1(d) is strictly decreasing, giving a unique upper-bound switch; series expansions independently checked symbolically give leading width coefficients (1-e^{-a})/2 and a/2. The standalone checker passed 894 assertions, which are corroborative rather than substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: Mass–volume curves are used for event pollutant interpretation and first-flush capture analysis. The theorem proves an exact, nonempty parameter regime where a two-source delayed runoff model has positive-negative-positive cumulative surplus despite decreasing individual source emission, which a universal one-exponent M(V) fit cannot capture even qualitatively. Exact source-weight thresholds, unique delay transition, and linear versus quadratic width collapse reveal when this ambiguity is robust or fragile. No empirical calibration or management performance is claimed.
